change: Removed oblique secondary (External Obliques + Internal Obliques). In a simple side-lying leg lift the torso is fully supported by the floor; obliques do not meaningfully fire as stabilizers. EMG research confirms Gluteus Medius as the dominant primary mover with TFL/gluteus minimus as assistants. Abductor secondary retained (covers TFL and gluteus minimus which co-activate during hip abduction but have no individual allowed mapping).
Same correction as side_lying_leg_lift_left: removed oblique secondary. In the floor-supported side-lying position the obliques do not provide meaningful stabilization. Abductor secondary retained.

Added Lower Back -> Erector Spinae as a secondary muscle. EMG research and multiple authoritative sources consistently cite erector spinae as a secondary stabilizer during the side plank isometric hold, resisting lateral trunk flexion and maintaining spinal alignment. Remaining secondaries (glutes Gluteus Medius, shoulders Lateral Deltoids, abs) verified and retained.

Added Lower Back -> Erector Spinae as a secondary muscle, consistent with side plank variants. The dynamic hip dip motion adds erector spinae demand eccentrically during hip lowering and concentrically during hip drive. Remaining secondaries verified and retained.

Added abs secondary (Upper Rectus Abdominis + LowerRectus Abdominis). Rectus abdominis is consistently cited as a secondary stabilizer in all side plank variants and the dynamic hip lift adds anterior core anti-rotation demand. Note: Lower Back (Erector Spinae) was omitted to stay within 5 secondary cap and abs are more directly cited; uncertainty remains whether erector spinae warrants inclusion for this variant.
